correctness.rationale: The exact count formula is a direct singleton choice. The full TP\(_2\) proof reduces adjacent minors to the identity \(r a_r^2-(r+1)a_{r-1}a_{r+1}+(N-1)(b_{r-1}a_r-b_ra_{r-1})\). The first summand is nonnegative by Newton ultra-log-concavity; the second by likelihood-ratio comparison of adjacent associated-Stirling coefficient rows, rigorously derived from Bóna–Mező Theorem 1 interlaced negative roots and the elementary Bernoulli-convolution log-concavity determinant. Edge cases \(N=0,1,2,3\) and feasible support intervals are explicitly handled. All minors follow from adjacent likelihood-ratio orders and transitivity. The strict stochastic and covariance statements follow from growing support maxima. The independent exact integer verifier passed 467,463 assertions (adjacent minors through \(n=75\), all minors through \(n=22\), and independent enumeration through \(n=8\)). The infinite theorem is proved analytically, not by finite checks.

originality.rationale: Novelty is assigned only to the exact finite-sample total-positivity and conditional likelihood-ratio ordering, not the known exact singleton count or nonsingleton-polynomial recurrence/interlacing. The full relevant Bóna–Mező Theorem 1 and Timashev (2003) primary formulas were compared at statement level. Timashev studies fixed-block-count size-r frequencies and asymptotic laws, without an ordering as the conditioning block count varies. Bóna–Mező proves one-variable real-rootedness and interlacing but does not establish the present two-variable TP2 minors; the new determinant decomposition and Bernoulli LR transfer are required. The published closest semantic result on unconditional block-size covariance at Lambert-W scale is strictly weaker/different. Priority remains qualified by possible indirect historical coverage.

value.rationale: The two natural statistics of a random set partition—number of blocks and number of singleton blocks—now have a sharp finite-n all-threshold dependence hierarchy, not merely a covariance or mean comparison. The bivariate TP2 property gives strict dependence for all increasing functions and survives arbitrary positive Gibbs weighting on total block count. This structural synthesis of real-rootedness, interlacing and adjacent-minor decomposition is mathematically motivated by richness-conditioned occupancy and yields a complete ordering absent from known univariate and asymptotic treatments.
